means: Point of view - the frame IS a character's eyes. On danbooru it almost always arrives attached to the viewer's own body: pov hands, pov feet, and the subject looking straight at the viewer.
does: On its own, nothing useful here. The shot_framing_type pov panel - clause "pov, first-person view, pov hands" - came back as an ordinary third-person medium shot of the boy. No hands, no first-person geometry, nothing. "first-person view" is prose the model has never seen, and "pov hands" needs a hand it can attach to something. This is another counting-and-framing instruction rather than a description: it makes a claim about where the viewer's body is, and if the rest of the prompt does not agree, the claim is dropped.
reach_for_it: if you must have it, build it from nouns instead: "looking at viewer, eye contact" plus a real foreground object the hands can hold - "hand in foreground, holding a phone". The bare tag will not do it.
used_in: shot.framing_type pov. Do not confuse it with story.pov, which is a story-level variable naming whose experience the scene follows and never reaches the prompt at all.
example_base: 1boy, solo, male focus, short black hair, dark jacket, standing on a rooftop, city skyline behind, late afternoon sun, looking away, masterpiece, best quality, very aesthetic, absurdres
read_it_as: Compare the SHADING, colour and line - not the pose or framing. Adding any clause re-rolls the model's conditioning, so composition moves between the two panels even at a fixed seed. An img2img pass from one fixed base image would isolate the tag properly; that is not built yet.
